Definition: from G601; disclosure:--appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be revealed, revelation.
BiblicalUsage: A disclosure, an unveiling — the word the last book of the Bible takes for its title. Paul received his gospel not from man but by the revelation of Jesus Christ in Galatians 1:12, and by revelation God made known to him the mystery in Ephesians 3:3. The Corinthians wait for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ in 1 Corinthians 1:7, and Revelation 1:1 calls the whole book the revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to shew His servants things which must shortly come to pass.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that revelation is God pulling back the curtain, not man climbing up to peek behind it. The gospel was not worked out, it was shown; the end was not guessed, it was given. That is why I can trust both — the same God who unveiled the mystery also unveiled the last day.
